Team / Sophie / Latha — follow-up from today's sync. Below is the redline approach I will upload to the shared Drive (link above) and propose in the MSA redline document. I included rationale so sales/cs can map to commercial asks.

Proposed legal redlines (summary):
1) Defense control carve: Customer may elect defense control only where the alleged infringement arises exclusively from (a) Customer s proprietary training data or (b) Customer s instructions that materially alter the model s core architecture or weights, and not from Redwood s provided model weights or public model components. If Customer elects defense control, Customer shall: (i) promptly notify Redwood in writing; (ii) provide all evidence and counsel details; (iii) retain counsel reasonably acceptable to Redwood; (iv) indemnify Redwood for settlements/fees that are the direct result of Customer s control where Redwood s cooperation was not withheld.

2) Cooperation & evidence-preservation: Both parties must take reasonable steps to preserve relevant logs, data, and model snapshots once notified. We propose a 10-business-day preservation window during which parties must not delete or overwrite candidate artifacts; Redwood will provide a single point-of-contact in our SOC team for evidence requests; requests for custody require a written request and a limited transfer protocol.

3) Allocation & caps: Maintain Redwood s standard indemnity cap tied to the order form (express dollar cap), but carve out an enhanced cap for claims where Customer had defense control and the claim is a direct result of Customer s fine-tuning or added data (i.e., a 2x cap for those claims). This provides a commercial lever (price/term) for customers who require defense-control.

4) Insurance & mitigation: We ask the customer to represent they have commercially reasonable insurance and to notify insurers promptly. If Customer requires defense control without increased term/price, we will request evidence of insurance limits consistent with the deal profile.

Rationale: preserves Redwood s ability to defend model-origin claims while giving customers a pathway to defense control when the facts clearly point to customer-origin liability. Also creates commercial levers (price/term/insurance) to balance risk.

Next steps: I'll upload the tracked changes (Solace_MSA_Redline_v3.docx) to the link. Ben — if you can confirm the commercial trade buckets (term / ARR thresholds / insurance expectations) by EOD Wednesday, I'll finalize language for counsel. Sophie / Latha — please flag any absolute deal-stoppers in writing so we can escalate.

Kimberly Park
